title: The cholesterol-raising factor from coffee beans, cafestol, as an agonist ligand for the farnesoid and pregnane X receptors
authors: Ricketts ML, Boekschoten MV, Kreeft AJ, Hooiveld GJ, Moen CJ, Müller M, et al.
population: APOE3Leiden transgenic mice (30-day diet with 0.04% cafestol); wild-type, FXR-null, PXR-null and FXR/PXR double-knockout mice; transfected HepG2 and CV-1 cells

result: In APOE3Leiden mice, cafestol raised serum cholesterol by 40% and triglycerides by 62%. Cafestol activated the ligand-binding domains and full-length forms of FXR and PXR in cell assays and recruited the coactivator SRC-1. In wild-type but not FXR-null mice, cafestol feeding repressed hepatic CYP7A1, CYP8B1 and NTCP, without inducing hepatic SHP or other positive FXR targets; it induced intestinal IBABP and FGF15, the latter through both FXR and PXR, and PXR-dependent intestinal CYP3A11, ABCA1 and CYP27A1. Cafestol does not raise serum cholesterol in wild-type mice; the relevance of the FXR-SHP repression of CYP7A1 to humans remains to be established.
